title: Chelsea's £64m Bid for Alex Scott Rejected as Bournemouth Hold Firm on Star Midfielder
excerpt: The 22-year-old has turned down a new contract at Bournemouth, with Manchester United, Arsenal, and Liverpool also circling as the Premier League's midfield transfer market heats up.
body:
• Chelsea have had a £64m bid rejected by Bournemouth for midfielder Alex Scott, with the club valuing him at around £80m.
  • Scott, 22, has turned down a new contract offer from Bournemouth despite the club's willingness to include a release clause.
  • Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool, and Manchester City have all registered interest in the England squad member.
  • Bournemouth insist Scott will remain at the club for the 2026-27 season as they prepare for their first Europa League campaign under new manager Marco Rose.

Bournemouth have rejected a £64 million bid from Chelsea for midfielder Alex Scott, according to talkSPORT, as the south coast club dig in to keep their prized asset ahead of a historic first season in European competition.

The rejection came just hours after Chelsea completed a record-breaking £117 million deal for Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, signalling that Xabi Alonso's side remain hungry for further midfield reinforcements. Bournemouth have drawn a firm line, valuing Scott at £80 million and maintaining publicly that he is not for sale at any price.

Contract Rejection Signals Intent

Scott's decision to reject a new contract has intensified the speculation. Bournemouth first offered improved terms in March, reportedly including a release clause designed to give the player a guaranteed exit path. Scott turned it down, and talks have since stalled.

With two years remaining on the deal he signed when joining from Bristol City for £25 million in 2023, the Cherries are not under immediate pressure to sell. But every window that passes without a new agreement chips away at their leverage.

A Queue of Suitors

Chelsea are far from the only club tracking Scott. Arsenal had an enquiry rebuffed in June, according to BBC Sport. Manchester United, who have already signed Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £50 million and triggered Youri Tielemans' £35 million release clause at Aston Villa, remain interested but are reportedly unwilling to meet Bournemouth's valuation.

"Bournemouth's stance remains that they expect him to be their player next season even without signing a new contract."

— talkSPORT report

Liverpool's interest adds another dimension. Andoni Iraola, who managed Scott at Bournemouth before leaving at the end of his contract, is now at Anfield — and the prospect of reuniting with his former boss could prove tempting. Manchester City and Tottenham have also been linked.

The competition mirrors a Premier League midfield market that has reached extraordinary levels. Elliot Anderson's £116 million move from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City and Rogers' £117 million Chelsea deal — a record for a British player — have reset the benchmark for what clubs will pay for proven English talent.

Scott's Rapid Rise

Scott was a central figure in Bournemouth's best-ever Premier League campaign, with the club finishing sixth and qualifying for the Europa League for the first time. The former Bristol City academy product made 37 league appearances, earning recognition from England manager Thomas Tuchel, who called him into the senior squad in November and included him in the pre-World Cup training camp in Florida.

Although yet to win his first senior cap, Scott was instrumental in England's Under-21 European Championship triumph, starting in the final victory over Germany. At 22, he is widely regarded as one of the league's most exciting young midfielders — a box-to-box operator with the technical quality top clubs are paying ever-increasing premiums for.

"Arsenal had an enquiry rebuffed in June, according to BBC Sport."

Bournemouth's Balancing Act

The situation mirrors a familiar pattern for Bournemouth. The club have sold Dominic Solanke, Dean Huijsen, Illia Zabarnyi, Milos Kerkez, and Antoine Semenyo over the past two summers, cashing in on key players while climbing the table each season. Losing Scott would be a club-record sale but would strip new manager Marco Rose of his most dynamic midfielder as Bournemouth face the dual demands of domestic and European football.

Scott is currently with his teammates in Austria for pre-season training. Bournemouth's winger Eli Junior Kroupi is also attracting top-club interest, but the Cherries have told rivals both players are unavailable.

What Comes Next

Chelsea's opening bid fell well short of Bournemouth's valuation, but the Blues have shown with the Rogers deal that they are willing to break records. Whether they return with an improved offer — or whether Arsenal, United, or Liverpool make formal moves — could define one of the summer's most compelling transfer sagas. With the Premier League season less than a month away, the clock is ticking for all sides.
